The iPhone Duo hits stores tomorrow, and the anticipation couldn’t be higher. Pre-orders are backordered until January, although Apple has confirmed that limited quantities will be available for walk-in customers on launch day. Apple Stores are already preparing for big crowds, and basically everyone who’s tried one is ready to declare it the best foldable of the year. 

But those early reviews aren’t all glowing. There’s an issue with app compatibility, which should be solved relatively quickly. Some people have lamented the lack of a telephoto lens. And others took issue with the battery life.

However, the biggest issue by far is the lack of Face ID. Due to the complexity of the double-screen design and the TrueDepth camera system, Apple opted to use Touch ID as the only unlocking/authentication biometric on the Duo. That means more fumbling and less convenience when wearing gloves or holding a drink. But according to a report from Mark Gurman at Bloomberg, Apple is looking to solve this as soon as possible.

On his new Power On podcast, Gurman spills some details he’s heard about the next generations of iPhone Duo:

But here’s what I’ve heard. There are a few different features that Apple is already looking at for the iPhone Duo 2 and the iPhone Duo 3. One thing that Apple has been actively working on, is under display Face ID.

And you saw, they took a bigger step towards that with the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max this year, where they made the Dynamic Island much smaller. They moved more of the components under the display. I’m told there are iPhone Duo 2 prototypes at Apple already that have an under display Face ID sensor and camera on the outside screen.

None of that is a surprise, of course. Apple generally holds back features that either aren’t cost-effective or can’t be implemented in the way Apple wants. The Face ID issue is probably a little of both, so it could take a little longer to reach a production device. Gurman predicts that the issue will be solved “by the first update or the second update. So in the next two to three years or so.

With iPhone Duo stock limited and online delivery estimates already stretching into 2027, you could be waiting until next year to get your hands on one anyway. At that point, it might make more sense to just wait for the 2nd-generation model.

If you’re planning to buy a new iPhone, should you buy now or wait for Black Friday? With the iPhone Duo going on sale tomorrow, October 23, Apple’s latest lineup will be complete – but the newest models aren’t necessarily the best buys.

The Duo joins the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, although limited launch stock means getting Apple’s first foldable could require patience. Meanwhile, there are some excellent U.K. deals on the discontinued iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max as retailers clear remaining stock. If you want premium cameras and performance without paying the latest Pro prices, those older models are worth considering.

Apple rarely discounts its newest iPhones directly, and its 2026 price increases have made choosing carefully even more important. Black Friday may bring better offers, particularly through carriers and trade-in promotions, but a strong discount on the right phone can make buying now worthwhile.

In this guide, we explain whether now is a good time to buy each iPhone, which models are worth waiting for, and when to expect the best deals. We’ll help you weigh the appeal of Apple’s newest hardware against the savings available on older models.

Best and worst times buy an iPhone in 2026-2027: At a glance

Best iPhone deals right now

If you are based in the U.K. it is possible to buy unlocked iPhones on Amazon – and certain models are frequently discounted. If you can get a good discount it’s always a good time to buy.

We are currently seeing fantastic savings on the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max – you can pay up to £500 less than you would for the equivalent iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max. We expect to see similar deals over Black Friday in November.

Amazon is offering £20 off the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max if you are approved for an Amazon Barclaycard.

The worst time to buy an iPhone

This is generally in the weeks leading up to Apple’s September launch event, or in the early spring, when new models are expected to be announced. Buying just before a refresh means you could miss out on new features or pay full price for a model that’s about to be superseded.

The best time to buy an iPhone

This depends on where you live:

In the U.K., where most iPhones are sold unlocked and off contract, the biggest savings are typically available during major sales events such as Amazon Prime Day (usually in July and October, and occasionally in March) and Black Friday in late November. However, worthwhile iPhone discounts can be found throughout the year if you know where to look.

In the U.S., where people tend to buy iPhones through a carrier, the best time to upgrade is often during Black Friday when networks enhance their offers with larger trade-in values, bill credits, gift cards, or discounted service plans.

Should you buy a new iPhone now or wait?

Ida Blix

September and the months that follow are a much better time to buy an iPhone than earlier in the summer. July and August are usually poor months to buy a Pro iPhone because Apple’s September launch is so close. The iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo have now been unveiled, removing that uncertainty.

If you need a phone now, there’s little reason to wait for another annual refresh, and the iPhone 17, 17e and Air are also relatively safe purchases because their successors aren’t expected until spring 2027. See: iPhone 18 and 18e rumors and iPhone Air 2 rumors.

The iPhone 17 remains the strongest value, with a 120Hz ProMotion display, A19 chip, dual 48MP cameras and 256GB of storage for $899/£899 (although it was previously $799/£799). The 18 Pro and Pro Max make more sense if you want the best cameras, performance or battery life, while the Duo is for buyers specifically interested in Apple’s new folding design.

There is, however, one important reason to wait: 2027 could bring a much bigger iPhone redesign. Apple is rumored to be preparing a 20th-anniversary iPhone with a near-all-screen curved design, under-display Face ID, possible solid-state buttons, a thinner and more efficient OLED display, larger battery and major camera improvements. That could make 2027 a more significant upgrade year than 2026.

So if your current iPhone is still serving you well, waiting could be worthwhile. Otherwise, buy now if you need a phone, or wait until Black Friday if price is your main concern.

Wondering which iPhone to buy? Read: Best iPhone for our ranked recommendations and our iPhone buying guide for more in-depth information about cameras, displays, performance, storage, battery life and other key specifications across Apple’s current lineup.

When does Apple release new iPhones?

Apple has a well-established pattern of releasing new iPhones every year, typically in September. This annual cycle has been remarkably consistent for over a decade, with only rare exceptions.

While September remains the anchor for high-end models, Apple has begun to stagger its iPhone launches. Starting with the iPhone 16e in early 2025 and continuing with the iPhone 17e in spring 2026, Apple now releases more affordable models at separate events earlier in the year – often in March.

Apple announced the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo in September 2026, but their availability differed: the Pro models went on sale September 18, while the Duo goes on sale October 23. The standard iPhone 18, iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 are expected to follow in spring 2027.

September launches are usually accompanied by a dedicated Apple keynote, while spring releases are more likely to be announced via a press release although Apple has held spring events. Following the announcement, Apple typically opens pre-orders within a few days, with devices going on sale one to two weeks later. Initial availability can be limited, particularly for the most popular models and storage configurations.

Should you wait for the iPhone 18?

For most people, there isn’t a strong reason to wait for the iPhone 18. Apple isn’t expected to launch the standard model until spring 2027, so buying an iPhone 17 before the end of 2026 would still give you several months with Apple’s current mainstream model before its replacement arrives.

The iPhone 18 is expected to bring a 2nm A20 chip, potentially 9GB or 12GB of RAM, Apple’s C2 modem and possibly a new 24MP front camera. Extra RAM could prove particularly useful for future Apple Intelligence and Siri features. However, the rear camera system is still expected to consist of two 48MP cameras, while the display may remain broadly similar to the iPhone 17’s 6.3-inch ProMotion panel.

There is also some uncertainty over exactly what the iPhone 18 lineup will look like. A September 2026 rumour suggested Apple could effectively merge the standard iPhone and iPhone Air into a single model, rather than continuing them as two separate devices. If that happens, the iPhone 18 could adopt some of the Air’s thinner, lighter design while retaining the broader appeal of the standard iPhone. For now, though, that remains speculative.

Price is another consideration. With the arrival of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, Apple increased iPhone prices across the range, so the iPhone 17 now costs $899, $100 more than at launch. FAQ

1.

When is the best carrier upgrade timing?

Apple typically announces new iPhone models in September. Carriers often roll out their most aggressive trade-in offers and promotional deals around this time to entice customers to upgrade.

New releases: Waiting for the September (or spring) launch window is generally a good strategy if you want the latest model at a potentially better subsidized price.

Check your contract cycle: Many carrier contracts today last 24 to 36 months. If you’re nearing the end of your contract, you’re in a strong position to negotiate or take advantage of upgrade offers. However, upgrading mid-contract may involve paying off the remaining balance, so it’s worth checking your specific terms.

Consider Apple’s upgrade plans: Apple has replaced its old iPhone Upgrade Program with newer financing and leasing options. In the U.S., Apple Upgrade lets you lease an iPhone through Klarna and upgrade, buy or return it at the end of the term. In the U.K., Apple’s Flexible Finance Account offers eligible iPhones on monthly payment plans with the option to upgrade after a set number of payments. Terms and monthly costs vary by model.

2.

When does Apple update the iPhone?

Apple follows a well-established annual rhythm for its iPhone updates, with the primary event taking place in September each year.

Apple typically unveils its new iPhone lineup at a dedicated Apple Event in September. Pre-orders usually open on the Friday following the announcement, with devices shipping and arriving in stores a week later.

Apple also occasionally introduces new iPhones outside the September window and in the past it has held a Spring Apple Event at which more affordable iPhones have launched. The iPhone 17e, for example, arrived in March 2026, and the iPhone 16e launched in February 2025.

Compatible iPhone models also get a yearly operating system software update with new features that can make your old iPhone feel new again. The major iOS updates follow the September schedule.

Read our guide to the next Apple event to find out if an Apple event is imminent.

3.

When do iPhone prices drop and by how much?

Based on past experience, Apple is very unlikely to reduce the price of a new iPhone during its first year on sale.

However, when Apple introduces a new generation of iPhones, it usually cuts the price of the previous year’s models. That means September has traditionally been the point when older iPhones become cheaper.

Apple also tends to keep launch prices broadly similar from one generation to the next, at least in the U.S., although exchange rates and other regional factors can affect pricing elsewhere.

In 2024, for example, Apple reduced the price of the iPhone 15 and iPhone 15 Plus by $100/£100 when the iPhone 16 and 16 Plus arrived. The iPhone 16 also fell in price following the launch of the iPhone 17 in 2025. However, because the iPhone 17 doubled the base storage to 256GB, the older iPhone 16 looked less attractive even at $100/£100 less.

In 2026, the pattern changed. Apple actually raised iPhone prices, blaming higher memory costs. Even the year-old iPhone 17 and two-year-old iPhone 16 increased by $100, showing that older iPhones don’t always become cheaper when a new generation arrives.

4.

Is it better to buy from Apple or a carrier?

In the U.S., buying from Apple is usually the better option if you value flexibility. If you pay in full or use Apple’s own financing, the iPhone is unlocked, so you can switch carriers or use another eSIM when traveling. Apple also accepts trade-ins and, importantly, many AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon promotions are available when buying through Apple.

However, an iPhone bought from Apple but financed through an AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon device-payment plan is locked to that carrier until it has been paid off. An iPhone bought outright from Apple isn’t.

The main reason to buy directly from AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon is to take advantage of a particularly good promotion. U.S. carriers frequently advertise large trade-in credits or “free” iPhones, especially when you add a line or switch networks. The catch is that the discount is usually provided as monthly bill credits over 24 or 36 months, so if you leave early you can lose the remaining credits.

In the U.K., Apple sells iPhones unlocked and SIM-free, allowing you to shop separately for a SIM-only plan from EE, Vodafone, O2, Three or an MVNO. This makes it easier to switch networks and can work out cheaper over the life of the phone than bundling the handset and airtime into a single contract.

Apple isn’t necessarily the cheapest place to buy, however. Amazon U.K. and other retailers frequently discount SIM-free iPhones, and there can be substantial savings during sales events such as Black Friday.

Networks can also offer compelling promotions, including enhanced trade-in values, discounted airtime, generous data allowances or lower monthly payments. But make sure you compare the total cost of the contract, rather than focusing on the headline monthly price.

5.

When are the best iPhone deals?

The earliest you could expect to get a discount on the newest iPhones is around Black Friday at the end of November, so you might be planning to hold out until then. However, the deals we tend to see, if any, are usually for older handsets. See our round-up of Best Black Friday iPhone deals for more.

Nor should you expect to get a discount in an Apple Black Friday sale. Apple’s Black Friday sale usually only takes the form of vouchers with select product purchases, rather than a discount, and it is unlikely that the newest iPhone would qualify as in previous year’s new iPhones haven’t been included.

Note that while shopping events like Black Friday get all the attention, that’s not the only time you can get discounts on Apple products: we see discounts all the time. Another event where we see good iPhone deals is Prime Day, which happens in June or July and October every year. So take a look at the iPhone deals for Amazon Prime Day sale to see what you might be able to save.

In our experience, we don’t tend to see discounts on the newest handset until the spring – and these are always from third-party resellers, never from Apple. In fact, we don’t tend to see the iPhone discounted in the U.S. very often, most of the discounts we see are in the U.K. where unlocked iPhones are often sold off-contract at a good discount.

6.

Is it worth buying a refurbished iPhone?

Yes, buying a refurbished iPhone is absolutely worth it for most people, especially if you want to save money without sacrificing quality.

Buying refurbished is a great way to “pick up a bargain” while still getting a premium device. You can typically save 15% to 30% compared to buying new, and sometimes much more on older models.

A common misconception is that refurbished is the same as buying a used phone from a stranger, though. It’s not. A used phone is sold “as-is,” with no guarantee it will work properly. A refurbished phone has been professionally inspected, tested, and repaired if needed, and it comes with a warranty.

If you want the highest quality, Apple’s own refurbished store is the gold standard.

Conclusion: When is the best time to buy a new iPhone?

The worst time to buy is usually between July or August, mainly because with new iPhones on the horizon the price of the older handsets are likely to drop very soon.

If you want the newest iPhones then the best deals don’t tend to come before the spring and summer months. If you are happy to buy an older iPhone then you will probably see decent deals around Prime Day and Black Friday – but deals happen all year round. 

We hope this article has proved helpful in reaching an informed buying decision. Remember that good prices can be found all year round, if a retailer is feeling generous and you know where to look: read our guide to the best iPhone deals for more on that.

Its main advantages are the A18 chip with Apple Intelligence support, versatile dual-camera system, and Camera Control and Action buttons. It remains fast and capable, but its 128GB of base storage and older 60Hz display make it much less appealing at anything close to the price of newer models. 

That means the decision comes down largely to discounts. Black Friday and clearance sales are likely to offer the best opportunities. If the iPhone 16 is only slightly cheaper than an iPhone 17e or iPhone 17, skip it. If you can find it heavily discounted, however, it can still represent excellent value.

Read our full Apple iPhone 16 review

FAQ

1.

When is the best carrier upgrade timing?

Apple typically announces new iPhone models in September. Carriers often roll out their most aggressive trade-in offers and promotional deals around this time to entice customers to upgrade.

New releases: Waiting for the September (or spring) launch window is generally a good strategy if you want the latest model at a potentially better subsidized price.

Check your contract cycle: Many carrier contracts today last 24 to 36 months. If you’re nearing the end of your contract, you’re in a strong position to negotiate or take advantage of upgrade offers. However, upgrading mid-contract may involve paying off the remaining balance, so it’s worth checking your specific terms.

Consider Apple’s upgrade plans: Apple has replaced its old iPhone Upgrade Program with newer financing and leasing options. In the U.S., Apple Upgrade lets you lease an iPhone through Klarna and upgrade, buy or return it at the end of the term. In the U.K., Apple’s Flexible Finance Account offers eligible iPhones on monthly payment plans with the option to upgrade after a set number of payments. Terms and monthly costs vary by model.

2.

When does Apple update the iPhone?

Apple follows a well-established annual rhythm for its iPhone updates, with the primary event taking place in September each year.

Apple typically unveils its new iPhone lineup at a dedicated Apple Event in September. Pre-orders usually open on the Friday following the announcement, with devices shipping and arriving in stores a week later.

Apple also occasionally introduces new iPhones outside the September window and in the past it has held a Spring Apple Event at which more affordable iPhones have launched. The iPhone 17e, for example, arrived in March 2026, and the iPhone 16e launched in February 2025.

Compatible iPhone models also get a yearly operating system software update with new features that can make your old iPhone feel new again. The major iOS updates follow the September schedule.

Read our guide to the next Apple event to find out if an Apple event is imminent.

3.

When do iPhone prices drop and by how much?

Based on past experience, Apple is very unlikely to reduce the price of a new iPhone during its first year on sale.

However, when Apple introduces a new generation of iPhones, it usually cuts the price of the previous year’s models. That means September has traditionally been the point when older iPhones become cheaper.

Apple also tends to keep launch prices broadly similar from one generation to the next, at least in the U.S., although exchange rates and other regional factors can affect pricing elsewhere.

In 2024, for example, Apple reduced the price of the iPhone 15 and iPhone 15 Plus by $100/£100 when the iPhone 16 and 16 Plus arrived. The iPhone 16 also fell in price following the launch of the iPhone 17 in 2025. However, because the iPhone 17 doubled the base storage to 256GB, the older iPhone 16 looked less attractive even at $100/£100 less.

In 2026, the pattern changed. Apple actually raised iPhone prices, blaming higher memory costs. Even the year-old iPhone 17 and two-year-old iPhone 16 increased by $100, showing that older iPhones don’t always become cheaper when a new generation arrives.

4.

Is it better to buy from Apple or a carrier?

In the U.S., buying from Apple is usually the better option if you value flexibility. If you pay in full or use Apple’s own financing, the iPhone is unlocked, so you can switch carriers or use another eSIM when traveling. Apple also accepts trade-ins and, importantly, many AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon promotions are available when buying through Apple.

However, an iPhone bought from Apple but financed through an AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon device-payment plan is locked to that carrier until it has been paid off. An iPhone bought outright from Apple isn’t.

The main reason to buy directly from AT&T, T-Mobile or Verizon is to take advantage of a particularly good promotion. U.S. carriers frequently advertise large trade-in credits or “free” iPhones, especially when you add a line or switch networks. The catch is that the discount is usually provided as monthly bill credits over 24 or 36 months, so if you leave early you can lose the remaining credits.

In the U.K., Apple sells iPhones unlocked and SIM-free, allowing you to shop separately for a SIM-only plan from EE, Vodafone, O2, Three or an MVNO. This makes it easier to switch networks and can work out cheaper over the life of the phone than bundling the handset and airtime into a single contract.

Apple isn’t necessarily the cheapest place to buy, however. Amazon U.K. and other retailers frequently discount SIM-free iPhones, and there can be substantial savings during sales events such as Black Friday.

Networks can also offer compelling promotions, including enhanced trade-in values, discounted airtime, generous data allowances or lower monthly payments. But make sure you compare the total cost of the contract, rather than focusing on the headline monthly price.

5.

When are the best iPhone deals?

The earliest you could expect to get a discount on the newest iPhones is around Black Friday at the end of November, so you might be planning to hold out until then. However, the deals we tend to see, if any, are usually for older handsets. See our round-up of Best Black Friday iPhone deals for more.

Nor should you expect to get a discount in an Apple Black Friday sale. Apple’s Black Friday sale usually only takes the form of vouchers with select product purchases, rather than a discount, and it is unlikely that the newest iPhone would qualify as in previous year’s new iPhones haven’t been included.

Note that while shopping events like Black Friday get all the attention, that’s not the only time you can get discounts on Apple products: we see discounts all the time. Another event where we see good iPhone deals is Prime Day, which happens in June or July and October every year. So take a look at the iPhone deals for Amazon Prime Day sale to see what you might be able to save.

In our experience, we don’t tend to see discounts on the newest handset until the spring – and these are always from third-party resellers, never from Apple. In fact, we don’t tend to see the iPhone discounted in the U.S. very often, most of the discounts we see are in the U.K. where unlocked iPhones are often sold off-contract at a good discount.

6.

Is it worth buying a refurbished iPhone?

Yes, buying a refurbished iPhone is absolutely worth it for most people, especially if you want to save money without sacrificing quality.

Buying refurbished is a great way to “pick up a bargain” while still getting a premium device. You can typically save 15% to 30% compared to buying new, and sometimes much more on older models.

A common misconception is that refurbished is the same as buying a used phone from a stranger, though. It’s not. A used phone is sold “as-is,” with no guarantee it will work properly. A refurbished phone has been professionally inspected, tested, and repaired if needed, and it comes with a warranty.

If you want the highest quality, Apple’s own refurbished store is the gold standard.

Conclusion: When is the best time to buy a new iPhone?

The worst time to buy is usually between July or August, mainly because with new iPhones on the horizon the price of the older handsets are likely to drop very soon.

If you want the newest iPhones then the best deals don’t tend to come before the spring and summer months. If you are happy to buy an older iPhone then you will probably see decent deals around Prime Day and Black Friday – but deals happen all year round. 

We hope this article has proved helpful in reaching an informed buying decision. Remember that good prices can be found all year round, if a retailer is feeling generous and you know where to look: read our guide to the best iPhone deals for more on that.

The MacBook Pro, as we know it, isn’t long for Apple’s Mac lineup. It’s expected to undergo a drastic change during next week’s “Pro and Tell” event. At long last, Apple is expected to unveil its long-rumored MacBook Pro that finally brings touchscreen support to the Mac.

A touchscreen alone, however, isn’t enough to sell me on an upgrade. I already have an iPhone and an iPad. For one, Apple needs to convince me that I even want a touchscreen on my MacBook Pro, but more than that, the touchscreen makeover is a perfect opportunity for Apple to upgrade its laptop in other ways. Here’s what I’ll be looking for when Apple unveils the first touchscreen MacBook Pro next week.

A new macOS

To be completely honest, I’m not really excited about a touchscreen on a MacBook Pro. I’m unable to imagine how the way I use my Mac can be enhanced by my fingers on the display. So this is the number one thing I’ll be looking for, way above anything else: I want to see how Apple plans to implement touch input in macOS.

It has to be more than, say, being able to tap and drag Safari tabs with accompanying visual effects, as was leaked recently. I need to see more than larger elements to accompany touch. I need to see features that will make me want to reach out and poke my display and think the inevitable fingerprints are worth it. For example, in a conversation here in the Macworld office, Jason Cross mused that iPhone Mirroring could have some advantages if you’re able to physically interact with the projection as you would the device itself. That’s the kind of interesting and novel new feature I’d like to see.

Touchscreen laptops aren’t a new idea, which means Apple has had plenty of time to experiment and develop a touch UI. But lots of people, including many who should be the target audience for a MacBook Pro, have used macOS for years and will need to see something truly innovative to consider buying one. I hope I see that next week, though I won’t be surprised if we have to wait until WWDC next June to see some real change.

Lighter design

The other day at the Macworld office, I had my 16-inch MacBook Pro in my backpack. I put my backpack on my desk, and it made a noticeable “thud.” Our office manager (an unabashed PC user) jokingly asked me why I carry a boat anchor around. I laughed, but he’s right: the MacBook Pro is very heavy.

Foundry

The 14-inch MacBook Pro weighs about 3.6 pounds (1.62 kg), while the 16-inch model is nearly 5 pounds (2.15 kg). By comparison, the 16-inch HP OmniBook 7 is about a half-pound lighter. Rumors suggest that the new model will be significantly lighter than the current crop of MacBook Pros, so I’ll be looking closely at the tech specs to see just how much they weigh.

But a lighter MacBook Pro also needs to keep the same battery life, which is one of the best features of the MacBook Pro. A thinner and lighter battery is fine as long as Apple doesn’t sacrifice the existing battery life that has become the hallmark of Apple’s flagship laptops.

Face ID

Touch ID is great, but Face ID is better because it’s less disruptive and more immediate. A year ago, a report claimed that Face ID on a MacBook is “years away,” but plans tend to change very quickly in the tech world.

Back when Apple introduced the notch with the first M1 Pro/Max MacBook Pro, it seemed to be an obvious placeholder for an inevitable upgrade to Face ID. Five years later, that still hasn’t happened. This new MacBook Pro—which is expected to ditch the notch for an iPhone-like Dynamic Island—is a perfect opportunity to bring the convenience of facial recognition to the only camera you’re always staring at.

Foundry

5G connectivity

Apple once thought Macs and touchscreens should not go together, and it’s apparently changed its mind. Maybe it’s also changed its longstanding opinion that cellular connectivity doesn’t belong on a laptop. If hell is freezing over with the addition of a touchscreen to the MacBook Pro, why not add 5G connectivity too? Now that Apple has its own C-series modems that are super efficient and work with its own silicon without worry of battery life or connectivity issues, there’s no reason why Apple can’t offer the option to add 5G to the next MacBook Pro, just as it does with the iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch.

A convertible 2-in-1

I’m not really sure what Apple has in store for the new design rumored for the touchscreen MacBook Pro, but my editor, Michael Simon, is wondering if Apple will do something truly different: Add a 360-degree hinge to turn it into a true macOS tablet. Apple has had a lot of time to work on its hinge tech with the iPhone Duo, so the touchscreen MacBook Pro could introduce something entirely new.

We’ve written for years about how the iPad hardware would be a perfect vehicle for a redesigned macOS for touch, and it would be interesting to see what a true tablet-ized version of macOS would look like. Could it support Apple Pencil? Will there be a virtual keyboard? As I said before, reaching out to touch my MacBook’s screen isn’t something I’m all that interested in, but a convertible design sure sounds tempting.

Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, officially goes on sale Friday, October 23, but getting hold of one could prove difficult. Preorders opened on October 16 and delivery estimates slipped rapidly, with Macworld’s U.S. tracking showing waits stretching to January 25, 2027 within around half an hour. Apple is still accepting orders, but there is another option for buyers who don’t want to wait: Apple has confirmed that limited numbers of the iPhone Duo will be available for walk-in customers at Apple Stores in the U.S., U.K. and other selected markets on launch day. Supplies are expected to be extremely limited, however, and there’s no guarantee of getting one without a preorder. Prices start at $1,999/£1,999.

The Duo opens like a book from a compact 5.4-inch phone into a much larger 7.6-inch device. Apple describes the internal screen as its largest-ever iPhone display, with 50 percent more screen area than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, while the outer display provides more than 90 percent of the screen area of an iPhone 18 Pro.

The biggest difference is obviously the folding design, but Apple has done more than simply add a hinge. The iPhone Duo ships with iOS 27.1, which adapts to different positions and orientations with fold-specific interface and multitasking features. These include Split View, hands-free FaceTime and video, StandBy without charging, and layouts that move seamlessly between the two screens. Apple Pencil USB-C support is also coming later in 2026.

The other major changes are the 7.6-inch nano-texture inner display, Touch ID replacing Face ID, an A20 Pro processor with vapor-chamber cooling, and a dual-battery system designed around the two halves of the phone. Apple has also introduced camera features that exploit the second screen, including Duo Preview, Smart Take, Kid Cue and Duo FaceTime.

Much of the pre-launch reporting proved accurate: the Duo name, book-style design, roughly 7.7- and 5.4-inch screens, Touch ID, two 48MP rear cameras, two front-facing cameras, A20 Pro, C2 modem, MagSafe and the white/dark-blue colors were all anticipated.

iPhone Duo at a glance

  • Apple’s first folding iPhone, with 5.4-inch outer and 7.6-inch inner displays.
  • Touch ID replaces Face ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button.
  • A20 Pro with vapor-chamber cooling, including a new 2nm manufacturing process.
  • Dual-battery architecture, giving up to 44 hours of video playback on the outer display.
  • Fold-specific iOS and camera features, including Split View, Duo Preview, Smart Take, Kid Cue and hands-free use.

iPhone Duo: Top 10 features

iPhone Duo release date: When will it go on sale?

Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo on September 9, 2026, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, but its first foldable iPhone won’t reach customers until October 23.

Preorders opened on Friday, October 16, at 5 a.m. Pacific / 8 a.m. Eastern / 1 p.m. BST. Customers can order through Apple’s website or the Apple Store app, choosing from Star White and Night Sky finishes and 256GB, 512GB, 1TB or 2TB of storage.

The October 23 launch covers more than 70 countries and regions, including the U.S. and U.K., with another 28 markets following on October 30. The Duo will also be available through Apple Stores, selected carriers and authorized retailers, although availability varies by market.

However, launch-day delivery allocations were exhausted quickly, and customers ordering now face a substantially longer wait.

Has the iPhone Duo sold out?

  • Initial delivery allocations sold out rapidly, but Apple has confirmed Apple Stores will have limited iPhone Duo stock for walk-in customers on October 23.

As of October 22, Apple was quoting January 22, 2027 for delivery of the 256GB iPhone Duo in the U.S. and January 25, 2027 in the U.K. Estimates can change and depend on the configuration and delivery location.

Apple has confirmed that its stores will have limited iPhone Duo stock for walk-in customers when sales begin on October 23. That offers another possibility for buyers facing long online delivery waits, but availability is not guaranteed and will vary by store.

Apple described preorder demand as “nothing short of extraordinary” and said it was working to get devices to customers as quickly as possible.

Supply constraints may also contribute to the backlog. A late-September report claimed that Apple and its manufacturing partners were experiencing low production yields. Long delivery waits therefore reflect the balance between demand and available supply, rather than revealing how many phones Apple has sold.

iPhone Duo design: What does it look like?

Apple

The iPhone Duo uses a book-style folding design. Closed, it is unusually short and wide for an iPhone, measuring 84.1mm wide, 117.8mm tall and 11.3mm thick. Open it and the width expands to 164.6mm, while thickness reduces to just 5.2mm, making it Apple’s thinnest iPhone when unfolded (taking that mantle from the iPhone Air). It weighs 254g.

The outer screen measures 5.4 inches, while the folding inner panel measures 7.6 inches. Both are Super Retina XDR OLED displays with ProMotion up to 120Hz, Always-On display support and up to 3,000 nits outdoor peak brightness. The internal display also has a nano-texture surface designed to reduce reflections and make the crease less noticeable. The inner display also has a replaceable top cover layer. AppleCare+ lists replacement at $19, although it must be replaced by Apple rather than peeled off like a conventional screen protector. Apple has not yet published the price without AppleCare+.

The frame and hinge cover are made from Grade 5 titanium. Apple uses a mirror-polished finish on the enclosure and a micro-blasted finish on the 3D-printed hinge cover. Ceramic Shield protects the rear, while Ceramic Shield 2 protects the outer display. The phone retains an IP68 rating despite its folding construction.

Apple

There are just two colors: Star White and Night Sky, essentially confirming the pre-event reports of silver/white and a very dark blue. For more information read about the iPhone Duo colors.

Action button and Camera Control

There is Camera Control, giving access to exposure, depth, zoom, cameras, styles and tone. It can also launch the new Siri Camera mode.

However, Apple’s Duo doesn’t feature an Action button. The regular iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max retain both the Action button and Camera Control, so this is one hardware-control compromise of the folding model.

Accessories

Apple is also launching two dedicated accessories for the foldable:

  • The iPhone Duo Case at $79/£79
  • The Duo Folio with Kickstand at $129/£129

Both became available to order on October 16. And there are plenty more of the best cases for iPhone Duo in our test reviews.

Face ID, Touch ID and the notch

Perhaps the most surprising difference between the iPhone Duo and Apple’s other flagship iPhones is that there is no Face ID.

Instead, Apple has brought back Touch ID, with the fingerprint sensor incorporated into the side button. It works whether the Duo is folded or unfolded, and Apple Watch can also be used to unlock the device. This confirms one of the most persistent pre-launch rumors.

The internal display therefore does not need the TrueDepth sensors used for Face ID. Its FaceTime camera sits beneath the display and disappears when it isn’t being used, giving the inner screen a largely uninterrupted surface.

The inner camera itself is hidden below the display rather than sitting permanently in a visible camera cutout. And yet, despite this and the absence of Face ID, there is still support for Dynamic Island.

iPhone Duo cameras: What cameras does it have?

Apple

The Duo has a 48MP Dual Fusion camera system, comprising:

The Duo does not have variable aperture. Variable aperture is exclusive to the 48MP Fusion Main camera in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

The biggest camera features for iPhone Duo

Duo Preview

The outer screen can show a live preview while somebody else is being photographed, allowing the subject to adjust their pose and framing.

Smart Take and Kid Cue

Smart Take detects when everybody is ready and automatically captures the shot. Kid Cue uses animations on the outer screen to encourage children to look towards the camera.

Two-screen shooting

The folding design supports unusual shooting configurations, including using the main cameras for selfies or group photos while seeing the composition on the other screen. Duo FaceTime can also put nearby participants onto the outer display.

Other notable camera features include 48MP macro photography, a 2x optical-quality crop from the Main camera, an under-display inner FaceTime camera, Dual Capture for simultaneous front-and-rear video, and 4K Dolby Vision recording at up to 120fps.

Rear cameras

The 48MP Fusion Main has an f/1.6 aperture, sensor-shift stabilization and can shoot 24MP or 48MP images. It also provides a 12MP, 2x optical-quality crop equivalent to a 52mm lens.

The 48MP Fusion Ultra Wide has a 13mm-equivalent lens, f/2.2 aperture and 120-degree field of view. It also supports 48MP macro photography and is the same Ultra Wide camera used by the iPhone 18 Pro family.

That means the Duo does not match the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max camera system. Those phones add a dedicated 48MP Fusion Telephoto and variable aperture on the Main camera, making the Pro models much more flexible for photography despite costing substantially less.

Pre-event reports were divided between a Main + Telephoto and Main + Ultra Wide arrangement. Apple ultimately chose Main + Ultra Wide, confirming the earlier reports that a dedicated telephoto could be sacrificed to save space.

Front cameras

On the outside is a 12MP Center Stage camera with an f/2.2 aperture. It supports Center Stage, automatic portrait/landscape framing, Dual Capture, Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5 and 4K Dolby Vision video at up to 60fps.

Inside is an under-display FaceTime camera with an f/1.8 aperture. Apple does not specify its megapixel resolution. It supports Center Stage for video calls and records at up to 1080p/60fps. Its major advantage is visual rather than photographic: the camera effectively disappears beneath the display when it isn’t being used.

iPhone Duo video features

The Main camera records 4K Dolby Vision at 24, 25, 30, 60, 100 or 120fps, with 4K/120fps also available for slo-mo. Cinematic mode reaches 4K/60fps and Action mode up to 2.8K/60fps. Dual Capture can record at up to 4K/30fps.

Apple’s specifications also do not list ProRes or Apple Log recording for the Duo. Those remain more Pro-oriented capabilities rather than part of Apple’s foldable camera proposition.

The Duo does support Spatial Audio recording, Audio Mix, Dolby Vision HDR and Apple’s computational photography features including Photonic Engine, Deep Fusion, Smart HDR 5, Photographic Styles 3, smart focus tracking and Apple Intelligence-powered editing.

Apple does not list conventional Spatial Video capture in the Duo specifications.

iPhone Duo processor: What processor does it use?

Apple

The iPhone Duo uses the A20 Pro, the same processor as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

It is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, a major step forward in transistor density and efficiency. Apple combines it with a new chip packaging design inspired by its M-series Mac processors. The package connects the A20 Pro directly to a custom vapor chamber to transfer heat away from the processor more effectively.

The A20 Pro includes:

  • 6-core CPU: two super cores and four efficiency cores
  • 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators
  • Dual 16-core Neural Engine
  • Hardware-accelerated ray tracing
  • A dedicated display engine capable of operating both Duo displays

Compared with the A19 Pro, Apple says the CPU is up to 20 percent faster, while the GPU is up to 40 percent faster and more power-efficient. The Dual 16-core Neural Engine delivers twice the compute power, while unified-memory bandwidth rises by 50 percent.

Apple also claims that the complete thermal system gives the Duo up to 35 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. That sustained-performance figure is particularly important for a folding device because prolonged gaming, multitasking and AI workloads generate considerably more heat than short benchmark bursts.

iPhone Duo RAM: How much memory does it have?

Apple has not disclosed how much RAM is inside the iPhone Duo.

Before launch, supply-chain reports consistently pointed to 12GB of RAM, which would make sense given the demands of running two displays, simultaneous applications, Siri AI and larger on-device AI models.

Apple does reveal that A20 Pro has 50 percent more unified-memory bandwidth than A19 Pro, which should help the Duo move data more quickly between the CPU, GPU and Neural Engine.

Extra memory is particularly useful on the Duo because iOS 27.1 can display multiple apps simultaneously and because Apple Intelligence and Siri AI increasingly run generative models locally rather than relying entirely on cloud processing.

iPhone Duo connectivity

Apple

Apple has put a significant amount of its own communications silicon into the iPhone Duo.

It uses Apple’s new C2 cellular modem, replacing Qualcomm silicon. Apple says C2 introduces AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability and supports mmWave 5G in the U.S.

The N1 wireless networking chip provides:

  • Wi-Fi 7 with 2×2 MIMO
  • Bluetooth 6
  • Thread networking

The USB-C port also supports USB 3 data transfers at up to 10Gbps and DisplayPort video output.

The Duo also has Apple’s second-generation Ultra Wideband chip, NFC and precision dual-frequency GPS.

It is eSIM-only worldwide, something that had been widely rumored before launch. Eliminating the SIM tray gives Apple additional internal space for its batteries.

iPhone Handoff – a feature introduced with iOS 27 – makes it easier to use an iPhone Duo alongside another iPhone without needing separate phone numbers. Both devices share your number, with calls, voicemail, messages and Find My location following whichever iPhone you unlock. Only one phone is active at a time. You could use the Duo’s folding display for work, then switch to an iPhone Pro when you want its telephoto camera. Should you buy an older iPhone?

Macwelt

Buying an older iPhone can be a great way to save money, but the key is choosing a model that still has plenty of useful life ahead of it. Apple typically provides around five to seven years of major iOS updates, with security updates often continuing for longer, so a relatively recent iPhone can remain perfectly usable for years.

We wouldn’t recommend simply buying the cheapest iPhone you can find. Very old models may technically run recent versions of iOS, but performance, battery condition and access to newer features can become increasingly compromised. We currently recommend avoiding anything older than the iPhone 15 Pro because even the iPhone 15 doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. You should definitely avoid models such as the iPhone XS and XR that can no longer run the latest iOS releases.

A refurbished recent-generation iPhone can offer particularly good value. You may be able to buy a former Pro model with better cameras and displays for less than a new entry-level iPhone. Buying from a reputable refurbisher is important, however: check the warranty, battery condition, returns policy and whether genuine replacement parts have been used. Apple’s own refurbished iPhones include a new battery and outer shell and come with a one-year warranty.

Our advice: A discounted or refurbished iPhone 16 or newer should offer an excellent combination of price, features and longevity.

Which iPhone has the best camera? iPhone 18 Pro

Apple

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have the best camera systems of any current iPhone. Both models use the same triple-48MP rear camera setup, so there is no photographic advantage to choosing the larger Pro Max unless you also want its bigger display and longer battery life.

The headline upgrade is the 48MP Main camera with variable aperture, which gives photographers more control over depth of field and should improve low-light performance. The Pro models also include a 48MP Ultra Wide camera and a 48MP Telephoto camera with 4x and 8x optical-quality zoom, giving them far more flexibility than Apple’s cheaper iPhones.

The standard iPhone 17 is still an excellent camera phone, with 48MP Main and Ultra Wide cameras, plus an improved 18MP Centre Stage front camera. For everyday photography it will be more than enough for most people, but it lacks the dedicated telephoto lens, longer zoom and advanced video features of the Pro models.

The iPhone Duo is more compromised. Despite its premium price, it has only two 48MP rear cameras and lacks a dedicated telephoto camera, variable aperture, ProRes and Apple Log. Its strengths are instead its fold-specific shooting features and dual-screen flexibility.

The iPhone Air and iPhone 17e are the least versatile, with just a single 48MP rear camera.

Our choice: If photography and video are your priority, buy the iPhone 18 Pro. It offers the same camera system as the Pro Max for less money and in a more manageable size.

Which iPhone has the best battery life? iPhone 18 Pro Max

Apple

The iPhone 18 Pro Max has the best battery life of any current iPhone, with Apple rating it for up to 45 hours of video playback. That puts it comfortably ahead of the smaller iPhone 18 Pro and makes battery life one of the strongest reasons to choose the Pro Max.

The iPhone Duo comes surprisingly close, with up to 44 hours of video playback when using its outer 5.4-inch display. However, battery life drops to around 31 hours when using the larger 7.6-inch folding display, so the Pro Max remains the better choice if endurance is your priority.

The iPhone 18 Pro is also excellent, offering up to 36 hours of video playback. That makes it a good compromise if you want strong battery life without carrying the much larger and heavier Pro Max.

Further down the range, the iPhone 17 offers up to 30 hours, making it the best mainstream option for battery life. The iPhone Air manages around 27 hours despite its exceptionally thin design, while the iPhone 17e reaches 26 hours.

The older iPhone 16 trails the current lineup at up to 22 hours of video playback.

Our choice: If battery life matters above everything else, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the clear winner. Its combination of a 45-hour rating, huge 6.9-inch display and Pro-level performance makes it particularly well suited to heavy users, travellers and anyone who wants to get through a long day without worrying about charging.

If your priority is spending as little as possible, choose the iPhone 17e which delivers excellent performance for $599/£599. Or seek out a refurbished iPhone from the Apple Refurbished Store or another place that sells refurbished iPhones.

Our choice: In terms of the features and hardware you get for every pound or dollar spent, the iPhone 17 is the sweet spot. For most buyers, it delivers the best balance of price, performance, cameras, display quality, battery life and longevity without paying for Pro-level features they may never use. Even better if you can find a iPhone 17 deal, then you are really getting a bargain.

Best iPhone for gaming: iPhone 18 Pro

Foundry

The iPhone 18 Pro is the best iPhone for gaming for most people, thanks to its combination of the A20 Pro chip, seven-core GPU and improved vapor-chamber cooling.

The A20 Pro is Apple’s fastest iPhone processor, but the cooling system is just as important for gaming. Better heat management should help the iPhone 18 Pro maintain high performance for longer during demanding games, rather than slowing down as the phone gets hot. Its 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display also provides smooth animation and responsive gameplay without making the phone excessively large or heavy.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers essentially the same gaming performance, but adds a much larger 6.9-inch display and significantly longer battery life. That arguably makes it the best choice for serious mobile gamers who value screen size and endurance, although it is heavier and costs more.

The iPhone Duo also uses the A20 Pro and has an enormous 7.6-inch folding display, which could be fantastic for some games, but its weight, price and unconventional form factor make it a more specialised choice.

Our choice: For most gamers, the iPhone 18 Pro offers the best balance of performance, cooling, display quality and portability. It’s the best choice if you prefer a more pocketable device but still want top-tier gaming power.

Best iPhone for seniors and older users: iPhone 17e

David Price / Foundry

For most older users, the iPhone 17e is probably the best choice, because it combines a relatively simple feature set with modern performance, strong battery life and a lower price than Apple’s flagship models.

Its 6.1-inch OLED display is large enough to make text, icons and controls easy to see without making the phone too bulky, while the A19 chip should keep it feeling fast for years. It also supports Apple Intelligence and starts with 256GB of storage, so there’s plenty of room for photos, apps and videos.

The iPhone 17 is a better option for someone who would benefit from a larger and more advanced display. Its 6.3-inch ProMotion screen, Always-On support and higher brightness can make scrolling, reading and outdoor use more comfortable. It also offers stronger battery life and better cameras, although it costs more.

We don’t recommend the iPhone Air, Pro Max or Duo for older users. The Air sacrifices battery life and camera flexibility for thinness, while the Pro Max and Duo are much heavier and considerably more expensive.

Our choice: iPhone 17e is the perfect choice for most older users.

Best iPhone for kids: iPhone 17e

Ida Blix

The iPhone 17e is the best iPhone for most children. As Apple’s most affordable current-generation model, it offers the best balance of price, performance and longevity, while being easier to justify than a flagship model if it gets lost or damaged.

It uses the same A19 chip as the iPhone 17, albeit with one fewer GPU core, so it’s easily fast enough for games, social media, schoolwork and Apple Intelligence. Battery life is strong, the 6.1-inch OLED display is a sensible size for smaller hands, and the 48MP camera is more than capable for everyday photos, even though it lacks an Ultra Wide lens.

The iPhone 17 is the better choice for older teenagers who care more about photography, video or display quality. It adds a 48MP Ultra Wide camera, a better front camera and a larger 6.3-inch ProMotion display, but costs considerably more.

A hand-me-down iPhone is also worth considering. It’s the cheapest option and better for the environment, provided you erase the phone first, create a Child Account through Family Sharing, and configure Screen Time and parental controls before handing it over. Read: How to set up an iPhone for a child.

Whichever iPhone you choose, those controls matter. In iOS 27, Apple is expanding Screen Time with new category-based Time Allowances, Ask to Browse, more flexible app schedules and improved contact controls. Communication Safety can also detect and blur sensitive, violent or graphic content.

For very young children, an iPad may still be a better first Apple device. By the time they reach 11 or 12 though, an iPhone becomes much more useful for staying in touch.

Our choice: iPhone 17e for most kids; iPhone 17 for older teens who want better cameras and display quality.

Should you buy an older iPhone?

Macwelt

Buying an older iPhone can be a great way to save money, but the key is choosing a model that still has plenty of useful life ahead of it. Apple typically provides around five to seven years of major iOS updates, with security updates often continuing for longer, so a relatively recent iPhone can remain perfectly usable for years.

We wouldn’t recommend simply buying the cheapest iPhone you can find. Very old models may technically run recent versions of iOS, but performance, battery condition and access to newer features can become increasingly compromised. We currently recommend avoiding anything older than the iPhone 15 Pro because even the iPhone 15 doesn’t support Apple Intelligence. You should definitely avoid models such as the iPhone XS and XR that can no longer run the latest iOS releases.

A refurbished recent-generation iPhone can offer particularly good value. You may be able to buy a former Pro model with better cameras and displays for less than a new entry-level iPhone. Buying from a reputable refurbisher is important, however: check the warranty, battery condition, returns policy and whether genuine replacement parts have been used. Apple’s own refurbished iPhones include a new battery and outer shell and come with a one-year warranty.

Our advice: A discounted or refurbished iPhone 16 or newer should offer an excellent combination of price, features and longevity.

Current iPhone lineup and prices

Here’s how Apple’s current iPhone lineup compares on price and the key specifications that are most likely to influence your buying decision.

The iPhone Duo goes on sale October 23, starting at $1,999/£1,999. Apple has confirmed limited launch-day stock for walk-in customers at its stores, while online orders may face much longer waits.

How to choose an iPhone

To help you narrow down the right iPhone model, we’ll look at the key questions that matter most when choosing an iPhone, including which has the best camera, battery life, display and performance, how much storage you need, and which model offers the best value.

Which iPhone has the best camera?

Apple

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max have the best camera systems of any current iPhone. Both use the same triple-48MP rear camera setup, so there is no photographic advantage to choosing the larger Pro Max unless you also want its bigger display and longer battery life.

The headline upgrade is the 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture, a first for the iPhone. You can switch between ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8 and ƒ/4.0, giving you more direct control over depth of field and low-light shooting. The Pro models also add a 48MP Ultra Wide and 48MP Telephoto camera, with 4x native telephoto and an 8x optical-quality zoom option. Apple also provides manual controls for aperture, shutter speed, white balance and histogram viewing, plus ProRAW, ProRes RAW and Apple Log 2 support.

The iPhone 17 remains an excellent camera phone for most people. It has a 48MP Main camera and 48MP Ultra Wide camera, plus a 12MP optical-quality 2x option cropped from the Main sensor. It also gains the 18MP Center Stage front camera, which can automatically reframe shots and supports Dual Capture. What you miss compared with the Pro models is the dedicated Telephoto lens, longer zoom range and more advanced pro photo and video controls.

The iPhone Duo also has two 48MP rear cameras, with Main and Ultra Wide lenses plus a 2x optical-quality crop from the Main sensor. Its folding design introduces some unusual camera features, including Duo Preview and Smart Take, but it lacks the dedicated Telephoto and variable-aperture Main camera found on the Pro models.

The iPhone Air and iPhone 17e are the least versatile current models, because each has only a single 48MP rear camera. Both can produce a 12MP optical-quality 2x view from the Main sensor, but neither has an Ultra Wide camera. The Air does at least get the newer 18MP Center Stage front camera, while the 17e retains a 12MP TrueDepth camera.

The older iPhone 16 sits somewhere in between, with a 48MP Main camera and 12MP Ultra Wide, plus the same 2x optical-quality crop from the Main sensor. It is still a capable camera phone, but the iPhone 17 improves the Ultra Wide to 48MP and upgrades the front camera.

Our recommendation: If photography and video are your priority, buy the iPhone 18 Pro. It gives you exactly the same camera system as the Pro Max for less money and in a more manageable size.

Which iPhone has the best battery life?

Mahmoud Itani / Foundry

The iPhone 18 Pro Max has the best battery life of any current iPhone, with Apple rating eSIM-only models for up to 45 hours of video playback, compared with 43 hours for versions with a physical SIM slot. Its larger battery and efficient A20 Pro chip make endurance a major reason to choose it over the smaller iPhone 18 Pro. However, modem hardware varies by region: according to iFixit’s teardown, the U.S. iPhone 18 Pro Max uses a Qualcomm modem, while Pro Max models sold elsewhere and all iPhone 18 Pro models use Apple’s C2 modem.

Apple rates the iPhone Duo for up to 44 hours of video playback on its outer display and 31 hours on its inner display. Early reviewers reported differing experiences: CNET found it comfortably lasted through a busy day, while The Verge questioned its endurance under heavy use.

If you want strong battery life without carrying the much larger and heavier Pro Max, the iPhone 18 Pro is an excellent compromise at up to 36 hours, while the iPhone 17 remains the best mainstream option at up to 30 hours.

Our recommendation: If battery life matters above everything else, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the clear choice. Its combination of a 45-hour rating, huge 6.9-inch display and Pro-level performance makes it particularly well suited to heavy users, travelers and anyone who wants to get through a long day without worrying about charging.

Which iPhone has the best display?

The iPhone Duo has the biggest and most distinctive display of any current iPhone. Opened up, its 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR OLED screen offers around 50 percent more screen area than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, making it especially good for video, gaming, reading and multitasking. The inner display supports 120Hz ProMotion, Always-On and up to 3,000 nits of outdoor brightness, while a nano-texture finish helps reduce reflections and make the fold crease less noticeable. There is also a 5.4-inch outer OLED display with 120Hz ProMotion and 3,000-nit outdoor brightness.

However, a bigger screen does not guarantee that every app uses the extra space effectively. Early reviews from Tom’s Guide and Wired found some third-party apps displayed black bars, while certain games had poorly fitting layouts. Apple has shared details of apps being optimized for the Duo’s launch, including Netflix, Prime Video and Fantastical. From October 23, look for the Made for iPhone Duo badge on App Store product pages. Support is still rolling out: Microsoft Word and Outlook updates are expected in the coming weeks, so check the current version of any app you rely on.

If you want the best conventional iPhone display, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is the standout choice. Its 6.9-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display combines an adaptive 1Hz to 120Hz ProMotion refresh rate, Always-On support and up to 3,000 nits of outdoor brightness. Ceramic Shield 2 provides additional protection, while Apple has also reduced the bezels and made the Dynamic Island smaller. The iPhone 18 Pro offers essentially the same display technology at a more manageable 6.3 inches.

You no longer need to buy a Pro model to get Apple’s best core display technology, though. The iPhone 17 and iPhone Air also support ProMotion and Always-On, features that were previously reserved for Pro iPhones. Both reach 3,000 nits outdoors, with the iPhone 17 offering a 6.3-inch screen and the Air a larger 6.5-inch display. That makes the iPhone 17 particularly strong value if you want a premium screen without paying Pro prices.

The older iPhone 16 and iPhone 17e are a noticeable step down. Neither supports ProMotion or Always-On, so their displays are limited to 60Hz. The iPhone 16 reaches up to 2,000 nits outdoors, while the 17e is dimmer still, with peak HDR brightness of 1,200 nits. The 17e also lacks the newer models’ ability to dim the display all the way down to 1 nit.

Our recommendation: Ultimately, screen size may matter as much as display technology. Choose the iPhone Duo if you want the largest and most versatile screen, the iPhone 18 Pro Max for the best conventional large-screen iPhone, or the iPhone 17 if you want most of the premium display experience for considerably less money.

Which iPhone is fastest?

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are the fastest iPhones you can buy, thanks to Apple’s new A20 Pro chip. The processor uses a 2nm manufacturing process and combines a six-core CPU with a seven-core GPU, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50 percent more memory bandwidth than the previous A19 Pro. Apple claims up to 40 percent faster GPU performance than A19 Pro. In our Geekbench AI testing, the A20 Pro’s Neural Engine delivered scores more than 40 percent higher than A19 Pro in the half-precision and quantized tests. These results measure specific AI workloads; doubling the number of Neural Engine cores does not mean every Apple Intelligence feature runs twice as fast.

The Pro models also benefit from a much larger vapor chamber and a new chip-packaging design inspired by Apple’s M-series processors. Apple claims these changes deliver up to 40 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro, which should matter most during gaming, video editing and demanding on-device AI workloads.

The iPhone Duo also uses the A20 Pro, but the shared chip does not guarantee identical performance. PCMag reported lower performance than the Pro models while finding everyday use and multitasking smooth. We’ll be carrying out our own testing to quantify the difference.

Further down the lineup, the iPhone Air uses the A19 Pro but with one fewer GPU core and less thermal headroom, while the iPhone 17 uses the standard A19 and the iPhone 17e a reduced-GPU version of that chip.

Our recommendation: For most people, all of these phones are more than fast enough. But if you want the best performance for gaming, video work or intensive AI tasks, the iPhone 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max is the clear choice.

Which iPhone is best for gaming?

The iPhone 18 Pro is our recommendation for most gamers, combining the A20 Pro chip with improved cooling. In our testing, it outperformed the previous generation’s A19 Pro by 93 percent in 3DMark Wild Life Extreme, 57 percent in Solar Bay and 53 percent in Steel Nomad Light. These are graphics benchmark results; the improvement you see in individual games will depend on the game and its settings.

In our review, we also noticed less heat buildup than on the iPhone 17 Pro during demanding games and other prolonged tasks. That was an observation during use, rather than a measured temperature reduction, and the phone still became warm.

Its 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion display also delivers smooth, responsive gameplay without making the phone especially bulky.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max offers essentially the same gaming performance, but its 6.9-inch display and much longer battery life make it the better option for gamers who prioritize screen size and endurance. Apple rates it for up to 45 hours of video playback, compared with 36 hours for the 18 Pro.

The iPhone Duo is an interesting alternative. It uses the same A20 Pro chip with a seven-core GPU and vapor-chamber cooling, while its 7.6-inch inner ProMotion display provides far more room for games. The trade-offs are its much higher price, 254g weight and folding form factor. Game optimisation is another consideration: early reviewers encountered games that did not fill the inner display correctly. Apple highlights Asphalt Legends among games taking advantage of the folding display, while the Duo-specific update for Zenless Zone Zero is scheduled for November. Check how your favorite titles handle its dimensions before paying extra for the larger screen.

The iPhone Air and iPhone 17 are still very capable gaming phones, but they sit below the A20 Pro models for sustained graphics performance.

Our recommendation: For most gamers, choose the iPhone 18 Pro; choose the 18 Pro Max if you want the biggest conventional screen and longest battery life.

Which iPhone is best value

The iPhone 17 is the best-value iPhone overall because it gives you the strongest balance of price, display, cameras, storage and battery life without paying Pro prices.

For $899/£899, you get a 6.3-inch 120Hz ProMotion Always-On display, the A19 chip, dual 48MP rear cameras, an 18MP Center Stage front camera, 256GB of storage as standard and up to 30 hours of video playback. That is a substantial step up from the iPhone 17e, which is cheaper but drops ProMotion, Always-On and the Ultra Wide camera.

The iPhone 17e is still the best budget choice if keeping the purchase price down matters most. It starts lower, still has the A19 chip and 256GB of storage, and offers excellent battery life, but its simpler display and single rear camera make it less complete.

Our recommendation: Choose the iPhone 17 for the best overall value, or the iPhone 17e if your priority is spending as little as possible.

How to choose the right iPhone specs

Choosing the right iPhone isn’t just about picking the newest model. You’ll also want to think about how much storage you need, what screen size feels comfortable, how much weight you’re willing to carry, and whether features such as ProMotion, advanced cameras, longer battery life or extra performance are worth paying for. The right balance will depend on how you use your phone: someone who mainly messages, browses and takes occasional photos will have very different needs from someone who shoots lots of video, plays demanding games or wants a large display for reading and media.

How much iPhone storage do you need?

Choosing the right amount of storage is important because you can’t add more internal storage later. iPhones don’t have a microSD card slot, so it’s worth thinking about how much space you’ll need over the lifetime of the phone before you buy.

The good news is that all of Apple’s current generation iPhones start with 256GB, including the iPhone 17e. That’s a much more comfortable starting point than 128GB, particularly as 48MP photos, 4K video, large games and system data all take up more space than they used to. It also makes the older 128GB iPhone 16 look like relatively poor value if it is only $100/£100 less than a newer model with twice the storage.

For most people, 256GB is the sweet spot. Before deciding, check how much storage you’re currently using by going to Settings > General > iPhone Storage. If you’re already close to your limit, move up a capacity when you upgrade.

Several things can quickly eat into your available space:

  • Photos and videos: 48MP photos and 4K video files are much larger than older formats.
  • Apple Intelligence: Apple’s AI features require several gigabytes of dedicated storage.
  • Apps and games: Some modern games can take up many gigabytes.
  • System data: iOS, caches and logs can consume a significant amount of space over time.

Which storage size should you buy?

  • 128GB: Only worth considering on an older discounted model if you mostly stream content and rely heavily on cloud storage.
  • 256GB: The best choice for most people, with enough room for apps, photos, videos and several years of use.
  • 512GB: Ideal if you shoot lots of 4K video, keep a large offline media library or install many large games.
  • 1TB or 2TB: Best suited to photographers, videographers and creators who regularly work with ProRAW or ProRes files.

Can you add more storage later?

No. You can’t upgrade an iPhone’s internal storage after purchase. You can, however, free up space with iCloud+, which lets you keep full-resolution photos and videos in the cloud while storing smaller optimized versions on the iPhone. You can also connect a USB-C SSD or flash drive to compatible iPhones to transfer files or, on supported Pro models, record ProRes video directly to external storage.

Our recommendation: Start with your current storage use and allow room for growth. For most people, 256GB is sufficient; choose 512GB or more if you keep large photo, video or game libraries locally. Pay for capacity you are likely to use rather than automatically choosing the largest option.

Which iPhone processor should you choose?

Apple

Apple’s A-series chips have consistently set the benchmark for smartphone performance, but the current lineup now spans several generations and performance tiers. At the top is the A20 Pro, which powers the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo. It is Apple’s first iPhone chip built on a 2nm process and features a six-core CPU, seven-core GPU, Dual 16-core Neural Engine and 50 percent more memory bandwidth than the A19 Pro. Apple says CPU performance is up to 20 percent faster than the A19 Pro, while GPU performance is up to 40 percent faster, with roughly double the AI compute performance.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are the best choices if you want maximum performance, particularly for demanding games, video editing or intensive Apple Intelligence tasks. Their larger vapor chamber and revised chip packaging also improve sustained performance, with Apple claiming up to 40 percent better sustained performance than the iPhone 17 Pro. The iPhone Duo uses the same full A20 Pro chip, including all seven GPU cores, although its folding design places greater constraints on cooling.

The previous-generation A19 Pro remains very capable. It powered the now-discontinued iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max and is still used in the iPhone Air. The Pro models used the full six-core GPU, while the Air has five GPU cores and less thermal headroom. The standard iPhone 17 uses the A19, while the iPhone 17e uses a cut-down version with a four-core GPU. Both are still more than fast enough for everyday use, multitasking, gaming and Apple Intelligence.

Our recommendation: For most people, processor choice shouldn’t be the deciding factor: even the A19 offers more performance than typical users need. Choose an A20 Pro iPhone if you want the fastest graphics, best sustained performance and strongest long-term headroom; otherwise, the A19 in the iPhone 17 offers the best balance of speed and value. For most buyers, the choice between models is likely to come down to cameras and other features rather than processor speed alone.

Finding the iPhone dimensions and design that suit you

Apple

Once you’ve narrowed down the features you need, think about which iPhone will actually be comfortable to carry and use every day. Screen size is only part of the story: dimensions, weight, thickness and materials can make two similarly sized iPhones feel very different.

The most distinctive model is the iPhone Duo. Folded, it is short and wide at 117.8 x 84.1 x 11.3mm, but opens to 164.6mm wide and just 5.2mm thick, with a 7.6-inch inner display. At 254g, it is also the heaviest current iPhone. It uses a titanium frame, has Touch ID in the side button, and keeps Camera Control but drops the Action button.

At the other extreme is the iPhone Air, which is only 5.64mm thick and 165g, despite having a 6.5-inch display. Its titanium frame and single rear camera make it the obvious choice if low weight and thinness matter more than camera versatility or maximum battery life.

The iPhone 18 Pro measures 150 x 71.9 x 8.75mm and 211g, while the 18 Pro Max is 163.4 x 78 x 8.75mm and 249g. The Pro Max is substantially heavier, so it’s worth handling one before buying. The iPhone 17 sits in the middle at 149.6 x 71.5 x 7.95mm and 177g, making its 6.3-inch display easier to manage.

Design differences

Most current iPhones include Camera Control, the touch-sensitive side control for launching the Camera app and adjusting settings. The iPhone 17e is the exception. The Action button is also standard on most recent models, although the Duo omits it.

The iPhone Duo is eSIM-only and cannot accept a physical SIM card. Check that your carrier and any travel SIM services you use support eSIM before buying.

Camera layouts vary too. The 18 Pro and Pro Max have three rear cameras across a broad Camera Plateau, the Duo and iPhone 17 use dual-camera systems, and the Air and 17e have a single rear camera.

Color choices vary by model, from understated finishes on the Pro and Duo to brighter options on the iPhone 17 and iPhone 16, so your preferred look may help narrow down the choice.

Durability

The newer iPhone 18 Pro models, iPhone 17, Air and 17e use Ceramic Shield 2 on the front, while the Air and Pro models also add extra protection to the rear. Current iPhones are also rated IP68 for water and dust resistance, but that doesn’t make them waterproof, so a case is still a sensible precaution.

Our recommendation: Choose the iPhone Air if portability matters most, the iPhone 17 or 18 Pro for the best balance of size and usability, the Pro Max for a larger screen and battery, or the Duo if you specifically want the foldable design.

Best way to buy an iPhone

There are several ways to buy an iPhone, each with its own advantages. The two main options are buying directly from Apple or through a mobile carrier. In the U.S., iPhones are typically purchased on a carrier contract and are often locked to that network. In the U.K., you can also buy an unlocked, SIM-free iPhone outright from Apple or other retailers, either at full price or with a discount.

Buy directly from Apple

Jon Stoa

Pros: You can get an unlocked, SIM-free phone (in most regions), access to the iPhone Upgrade Program, and the ability to trade in your old device for credit (up to $650). It’s also the best place to pre-order a new model for the fastest delivery.

Cons: You almost always pay full retail price.

Buy from a Carrier

Pros: This is where you’ll find the biggest discounts, often in the form of bill credits over 24 or 36 months when you trade in a phone and sign up for a qualifying plan. For example, AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon frequently offer up to $830–$1,000 off new iPhones with a trade-in.

Cons: These deals come with significant strings attached, including long-term contracts and specific plan requirements. Always read the fine print

A contract usually starts with an upfront payment that will vary depending on the iPhone model you go for and also how much you’ll be paying each month. That upfront payment is followed by monthly payments, normally for a total of 24 months, after which you own the phone (in most cases). Those monthly payments also cover data, minutes and texts.
